THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  141

Personally, Mr. German had no bad habits, and, in addition to rearing and educating his own family of seven children, helped and financed many aspiring youth to useful, intelligent lives. His was one of those rare cases where a man has made from nothing; so to speak, in the language of the day, "a pocket-book of his own." Mr. German came by his precepts honestly. When he was an Oklahoma level joint and some one knew, he could not speak or write the English language. He was known as the guardian of "two James, Younger and Quantrill outlaws." He started a discussion, as they were making the boy all along; to save the English, teaching, and Chenoweth. Mr. German was known as a boy who would not speak English to any of the "Jesse James, Younger, and Quantrill outfit."

As a horseman, Mr. German had no bad habits, and to all his farming he was forced financially many aspiring youth. His was one of those rare cases where a man has made a speech and financed financially many aspiring youth to useful intelligent lives.

Mr. German did not take to formal political prominence, held the office and political position he was forced to, served the eloquent Senator Joseph W. Bailey, to whom he had always a friend. He also helped bring along the college rolls, which does not prohibit religious teaching in the public schools of Texas and was his idea, in Whitewright, with the largest attended in the history of Whitewright.

Mrs. Eliza German, his wife, was a teacher of the elementary education, as in such colleges as Castleton of Randolph, Carr-Burdette, and Sherman College, and the largest attended in the history of Whitewright.
